title: probKFixed: Probability of Exactly k Fixed Points
content: probKFixed n k = C(n,k)·D(n-k)/n! is the probability that a uniformly random permutation of Fin n has exactly k fixed points. The numerator C(n,k)·D(n-k) counts such permutations: choose which k elements are fixed (C(n,k) ways), then the remaining n-k elements must be deranged (D(n-k) ways). The denominator n! is the total number of permutations. This is noncomputable because it uses real division.
significance: Defines the central object — the exact probability mass function for fixed-point counts — whose limit is the Poisson(1) mass function e^{-1}/k!.

title: Factoring P(X_n = k) via choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial
content: probKFixed_eq proves P(X_n = k) = (1/k!)·D(n-k)/(n-k)! for k ≤ n. This factorization is the key to proving convergence: the 1/k! factor is a constant, and D(n-k)/(n-k)! → e^{-1} by Mathlib's numDerangements_tendsto_inv_e. The proof uses Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial (C(n,k)·k!·(n-k)! = n!) via `field_simp; linear_combination D(n-k) * hchoose` to establish the polynomial identity.
mathContext: The identity C(n,k)·D(n-k)/n! = D(n-k)/(k!·(n-k)!) follows from C(n,k) = n!/(k!·(n-k)!). Lean technique: `linear_combination (numDerangements (n-k) : ℝ) * hchoose` after `field_simp` proves C*D*k!*(n-k)! = D*n! from C*k!*(n-k)! = n!.
significance: Reduces the k-fixed-point problem to the k=0 (derangements) problem by factoring out 1/k!, enabling a single application of numDerangements_tendsto_inv_e to handle all k ≥ 0.

title: derangements_rate: Alternating Series Bound (sorry)
content: The rate bound |D(n)/n! - e^{-1}| ≤ 1/(n+1)! is the alternating series estimation theorem applied to the Taylor series e^{-1} = ∑ (-1)^k/k!. Since D(n)/n! = ∑_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k! (proved by numDerangements_sum in Mathlib), the error is the tail ∑_{k=n+1}^∞ (-1)^k/k!, bounded by the first term 1/(n+1)!. This sorry exists because DerangementsConvergence.lean (which proves this result) has a pre-existing Mathlib API issue: `∑ k in S` should be `∑ k ∈ S` in modern Lean 4.
mathContext: D(n)/n! = ∑_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k/k! (partial sum of e^{-1} Taylor series). Alternating series theorem: |partial_sum_n - full_sum| ≤ |a_{n+1}| = 1/(n+1)!. Numerically: D(3)/3! = 1/3 (error 0.035), D(10)/10! ≈ 0.3678794... (error ~3×10^{-8}).
significance: The sorry is a mechanical issue (syntax update) rather than a missing mathematical idea — the underlying theorem is known and proven in the parent file. Fixing it requires replacing `∑ k in` with `∑ k ∈` throughout DerangementsConvergence.lean.

title: kFixed_tendsto: Convergence to Poisson(1) Mass Function
content: kFixed_tendsto proves P(X_{n+k} = k) → e^{-1}/k! as n → ∞. This is the Poisson(1) probability of exactly k events. The proof: (1) rewrite using probKFixed_succ_eq: P(X_{n+k} = k) = (1/k!)·D(n)/n!; (2) the limit is (1/k!)·e^{-1} = e^{-1}/k!; (3) apply tendsto_const_nhds.mul numDerangements_tendsto_inv_e — the product of a constant (1/k!) and a convergent sequence (D(n)/n! → e^{-1}) converges to the product of the limits. This proof is fully proved — no sorry required.
mathContext: The Poisson(1) mass function: P(Pois(1) = k) = e^{-1}/k!. Convergence: P(X_{n+k} = k) = (1/k!)·D(n)/n! → (1/k!)·e^{-1}. This is pointwise convergence of marginals. The stronger total variation convergence TV(X_n, Pois(1)) → 0 is proved in derangements-oq-03-oq-02.
significance: The core result: all k-fixed-point probabilities converge to their Poisson(1) values, completing the distributional convergence of permutation fixed points to Poisson(1). Fully machine-verified without the rate bound sorry.

title: kFixed_convergence_rate: Superexponential Convergence Rate
content: kFixed_convergence_rate proves |P(X_n = k) - e^{-1}/k!| ≤ 1/(k!·(n-k+1)!) for k ≤ n. The proof: (1) use probKFixed_eq to write P(X_n = k) = (1/k!)·D(n-k)/(n-k)!; (2) factor out |1/k!| = 1/k! (positive); (3) apply derangements_rate (the sorry) to D(n-k)/(n-k)!; (4) multiply by 1/k!. For d=365, n=10, k=1: rate = 1/(1!·10!) ≈ 2.76×10^{-7}, which is extremely tight.
mathContext: The bound factors as (1/k!)·(1/(n-k+1)!). Comparing: k=0 gives 1/(n+1)! matching derangements_convergence_rate; k=1 gives 1/(n!); k=2 gives 1/(2·(n-1)!). For large n, all rates are O(1/n!) — superexponential convergence.
significance: Gives quantitative control on the convergence to Poisson(1), showing the error decays faster than any exponential. The tighter bound for larger k reflects that conditioning on more fixed points reduces uncertainty.

title: kFixed_rate_tighter: Higher k Gives k! Improvement in Rate
content: kFixed_rate_tighter proves that for k ≥ 1: 1/(k!·(n-k+1)!) ≤ 1/(n-k+1)!. The k-fixed convergence rate is tighter than the k=0 (derangements) rate by a factor of k!. Intuitively: requiring exactly k specific things to happen (k fixed points) is more constrained than requiring 0 things (derangements), so convergence is faster. Proof: since k! ≥ 1 for all k ≥ 1, we have k!·(n-k+1)! ≥ (n-k+1)!, so 1/(k!·(n-k+1)!) ≤ 1/(n-k+1)!.
mathContext: Rate comparison: k=0 rate = 1/(n+1)!; k=1 rate = 1/(1!·n!) = 1/n!; k=2 rate = 1/(2!·(n-1)!) (better by factor 2 vs raw 1/(n-1)!). For same n-k: higher k always gives a tighter bound by factor k!.
significance: Confirms the monotonicity of the Poisson(1) approximation quality: conditioning on more fixed points improves the rate. This is consistent with the general principle that more constrained events have sharper probability approximations.
